summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -6 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar −; brl −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +4.0%; weakest: Lean hogs -15.8%. Key releases ahead: US Core Retail Sales m/m (11-17 8:30 AM ET); US Retail Sales m/m (11-17 8:30 AM ET); US FOMC Meeting Minutes (11-18 2:00 PM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.12% (+3 bp in a month), 2-year 4.83% (+9 bp); 2s10s curve +29 bp (-6 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.14% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.48 (+1.6% in a month, +5.3% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.783 (+13.5% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.666 (-0.4%); USD/MXN 18.43 (-0.1%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -4.5% in a month (+6.9% YTD); VIX 26.4. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 85.39 $/bbl (-13.8% in a month), Brent 92.59, ULSD 4.044 $/gal (-14.4%), natural gas 3.18 (-6.0%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -9.1% in a month, Shanghai Composite -3.5%, Hang Seng -2.8%, yuan +0.4% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 7 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (21%); S&P GSCI -10.9% in a month; gold -7.9%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
